newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Ex-Soviet Georgian water plant gets EBRD loan.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Soviet Georgian water plant gets EBRD loan.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) has allocated a $10 million, six-year loan to revitalise former Soviet Georgia's mineral water industry, an EBRD representative said Wednesday.
"This is the first EBRD financing of a private sector industrial project in Georgia," Oliver Descamps, director of the EBRD's Georgia team, told Reuters.
The loan is to the Georgian-Dutch JV Georgian Glass and Mineral Water Company (GG&MW), which holds an exclusive licence to produce Georgia's Borjomi mineral water.
"By providing GG&MW with a long-term debt facility, the EBRD would enable the Borjomi brand to be restored to its former market position," Descamps said.

He said the credit sent a signal to potential investors that private projects were feasible in the former Soviet republic, adding, "we expect the impact in terms of incremental flow of foreign direct investment into Georgia to be considerable."
